## Where we are

- Deck 02 measured differentiation ($F_{ST}$); deck 05 saw gene flow **erode** local
  adaptation.
- Now: what sets $F_{ST}$ in the first place — **divergence time** vs. **ongoing
  migration** — and the plant twist that breaks our diploid bookkeeping: **polyploidy**.
- **Today:** the split and island models, incomplete lineage sorting, and why polyploids
  need special care.

## Learning objectives

By the end you should be able to:

- Derive $F_{ST}$ under a **population split** and under **island–mainland migration**.
- Apply the **"one migrant per generation"** rule of thumb.
- Distinguish **incomplete lineage sorting** from **gene flow**.
- Explain why standard population genomics **breaks** for polyploids.

# How differentiation builds and erodes {.center}

## $F_{ST}$ from heterozygosities (recap)

$$
F_{ST} = \frac{H_T - H_S}{H_T},
$$

where $H_S$ = probability two alleles from the **same** subpopulation differ, and $H_T$ =
probability two alleles from the **total** population differ. Population structure makes
lineages **within** a deme coalesce sooner ⟹ $H_S < H_T$ ⟹ $F_{ST} > 0$.

## A population-split model — derivation

Two demes of size $N_e$ split $T$ generations ago, **no** subsequent migration. Within a
deme, $H_S \approx 4N_e\mu$. Drawing two alleles from the total (½ same deme, ½ different):

$$
H_T = \tfrac12 H_S + \tfrac12 H_B,\qquad H_B \approx 2\mu(T + 2N_e),
$$

since between-deme pairs cannot coalesce for $T$ generations, then take $\sim 2N_e$ more.
Substituting (and $\mu$ cancels):

$$
\boxed{\,F_{ST} \approx \frac{T}{T + 4N_e}\,}
$$

::: {.callout-important}
Under pure drift, differentiation grows with **divergence time** and shrinks with **$N_e$**
— deeper splits and smaller populations differentiate faster.
:::

## Worked example — divergence time

Two diverged plant populations (no recent gene flow): genome-wide $F_{ST} = 0.20$, and
within-population $\theta_W = 0.01$ per bp with $\mu = 7\times10^{-9}$/bp/gen.

. . .

$$
\theta_W = 4N_e\mu \;\Rightarrow\; N_e = \frac{0.01}{4(7\times10^{-9})} \approx 3.6\times10^{5}.
$$

. . .

$$
F_{ST} = \frac{T}{T + 4N_e} \;\Rightarrow\;
T = \frac{4N_e\,F_{ST}}{1 - F_{ST}} = \frac{4(3.6\times10^5)(0.2)}{0.8} \approx 3.6\times10^{5}\ \text{gen}.
$$

::: {.figure-prompt}
**FIGURE** — population split: one ancestral population diverging into two, allele
frequencies drifting apart with time (Coop, Fig 6.1).
:::

## An island–mainland migration model — derivation

A small island ($N_I$) receives a fraction $m$ migrants/generation from a large mainland.
Tracing two island lineages back, each generation they either **coalesce** ($1/2N_I$) or
one **migrates** away ($\approx 2m$). The probability they coalesce *before* either
migrates:

$$
F_{ST} \approx \frac{1/2N_I}{1/2N_I + 2m} = \boxed{\frac{1}{1 + 4N_I m}} .
$$

- Depends on $N_I m$ = **number of migrants per generation**, not $m$ alone.

## The "one migrant per generation" rule

| $N_I m$ | $F_{ST}$ |
|---|---|
| 0.1 | 0.71 |
| 1 | 0.20 |
| 10 | 0.024 |

::: {.callout-note}
A **single** effective migrant per generation ($N_I m = 1$) holds $F_{ST}$ near 0.2 — a
little gene flow goes a long way toward homogenizing demes. Contrast with the split model:
**history** and **ongoing flow** can produce the *same* $F_{ST}$.
:::

# Trees within trees {.center}

## Incomplete lineage sorting

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
- When populations/species split rapidly, lineages may fail to coalesce within each
  branch ⟹ **gene trees disagree** with the species tree.
- Pure **drift** — no gene flow needed. Most severe when internal branches are **short
  relative to $N_e$**.
- ⟹ A single locus is a poor guide to history; we need many.
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.figure-prompt}
**FIGURE** — ILS cartoon: a 3-taxon species tree with a discordant gene tree from deep
coalescence in the ancestral population.
:::

  B) "Illustration of incomplete lineage sorting producing gene-tree/species-tree discordance without any gene flow."
-->
:::

## ILS vs. gene flow

- Both produce **discordant gene trees** and shared variation — but with different
  **asymmetries**.
- **ABBA–BABA / Patterson's $D$** and **$f$-statistics** test whether discordance is
  symmetric (ILS) or skewed toward one pair (introgression).
- Plant introgression is rampant: ***Helianthus*** (sunflowers), oaks (***Quercus***
  syngameons), ***Populus***.

<span class="xref">→ ILS and introgression return in the Speciation Genomics module.</span>

# Polyploidy {.center}

## Whole-genome duplication is the plant condition

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
- **Autopolyploid** — duplication *within* a species (≥3 homologous copies).
- **Allopolyploid** — duplication *combined with hybridization* (divergent subgenomes).
- WGD is **pervasive** in plant history — every flowering plant is a descendant of ancient
  duplications; many crops are recent polyploids.
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.figure-prompt}

## Why standard popgen breaks for polyploids

- **More than two alleles per locus** — the diploid $p^2:2pq:q^2$ bookkeeping (deck 01) no
  longer applies; genotype classes multiply.
- **Polysomic vs. disomic inheritance** — autopolyploids can pair among all copies;
  **double reduction** sends sister-chromatid alleles to the same gamete.
- **Allele dosage** is hard to call from short reads (is it AAAB or AABB?).
- **Subgenome read-mapping** in allopolyploids collapses homoeologs ⟹ **inflated
  heterozygosity and $\pi$** if not separated.

::: {.callout-important}
Estimates of $H$, $\pi$, $F$, and $F_{ST}$ all assume diploidy. Apply them to polyploids
uncritically and the numbers are **wrong** — usually biased toward apparent excess
heterozygosity.
:::

## Polyploid examples and the path forward

- ***Tragopogon mirus*** & ***T. miscellus*** — allopolyploids formed in the last ~100
  years in North America — a natural experiment in genome merger [@soltis2004tragopogon].
- **Wheat** (allohexaploid), **cotton** (*Gossypium*), ***Capsella bursa-pastoris***
  (allotetraploid selfer).
- **Tools:** dosage-aware callers and ploidy-aware estimators (e.g. `polyRAD`, `updog`,
  `GENODIVE`); phase subgenomes before computing diversity.

## Summary — key equations

$$
F_{ST}^{\text{split}} \approx \frac{T}{T + 4N_e}
\qquad
F_{ST}^{\text{island}} \approx \frac{1}{1 + 4N_I m}
$$

- Differentiation reflects **divergence time** *or* **ongoing migration** — the same
  $F_{ST}$ has two stories.
- **ILS** mimics gene flow; asymmetry tests ($D$, $f$) tell them apart.
- **Polyploidy** voids the diploid assumptions behind every statistic in this module —
  handle ploidy explicitly.
